summary: Pushing a branch from a development checkout now signs its required checks first when they have no evidence, through a pre-push hook that never blocks the push

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes; this adds developer scripts, their tests and documentation, and one development-shell hook line.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes. No skip policy changes and every check stays enforce false; nothing skips because of the notes the hook writes.

compatibility.detail: No command, frame, scope or stored-format change in the product. The default development shell installs a git pre-push hook in the checkout, only when none of ours exists, no hook is set by another tool and core.hooksPath is unset.

downtime.detail: No startup work or expected interruption in any installed product.

manual.detail: No operator action is required. Developers can skip the hook for one push with ST_SKIP_EVIDENCE=1, or remove it with scripts/install-git-hooks --uninstall.

recovery.detail: No persistent product state changes or new swap-back restrictions.
